questions.prompt: Assume that a given Boolean function y = f(x1, x2, x3, ..., xn) where x1, x2, ..., xn are Boolean variables. Which of the following statements describes the satisfiability problem correctly?
options: It determines if y can be evaluated to 0 by any assignment of variables {x1, x2, x3, ..., xn}.
It determines if y can be evaluated to 0 by some assignment of variables {x1, x2, x3, ..., xn}.
It determines if y can be evaluated to 1 by any assignment of variables {x1, x2, x3, ..., xn}.
It determines if y can be evaluated to 1 by all assignments of variables {x1, x2, x3, ..., xn}.
questions.accepted: It determines if y can be evaluated to 1 by any assignment of variables {x1, x2, x3, ..., xn}.

questions.prompt: Assume that a given Boolean function y = f(x1, x2, x3, ..., xn) where {x1, x2, x3, ..., xn} are Boolean variables. In the worst case, how many input combinations need to be tried by a SAT solver?
options: Linear in the number of variables n
Polynomial in the number of variables n
Exponential in the number of variables n
questions.accepted: Exponential in the number of variables n

questions.prompt: Given a set of states S for a finite state machine (FSM), the problem of obtaining a set of states, S', that can be reached in one step from S is known as:
Which of the following statements is incorrect for Bounded Model Checking (BMC)
options: BMC tries to obtain a counterexample of a finite length n (n is the number of clock cycles from the initial state).
BMC lacks completeness because it considers counterexamples of a finite length.
BMC is useful in finding bugs if a bug can be obtained in a few clock cycles from the initial state.
BMC uses exhaustive simulation to find counterexamples of infinite length n (n is the number of clock cycles from the initial state)
questions.accepted: BMC uses exhaustive simulation to find counterexamples of infinite length n (n is the number of clock cycles from the initial state)

questions.prompt: Which of the following tasks is not a part of Combinational Equivalence Checking (CEC):
In which of the following cases port matching can fail during Combinational Equivalence Checking (CEC):
options: When some buffers are added to the netlist
When a NAND gate is optimized using Boolean algebra.
When the size of an inverter is increased to fix load violation
When an extra port is added to a design
questions.accepted: When an extra port is added to a design

questions.prompt: The Non-linear Delay Model (NLDM) models the delay of a combinational circuit element as a function of:
The setup time of a flip-flop in a technology library is modelled as a function of which two variables?
options: The voltage at the D-pin and Load at the Q-pin
Input Slew at the D-pin and Input Slew at the Clock Pin
Temperature and Input Slew at the D-pin
Input Slew at the D-pin and Load at the Q-pin
questions.accepted: Input Slew at the D-pin and Input Slew at the Clock Pin
